evidence.summary: Nine focused tests pass; neutral-CWD explicit workspace binds the expected Forge config and resident for each of two workspaces, with no cross-project attachment.
Explicit-config mismatch, multiple authoritative configs, and missing config produce precise fail-closed results; CWD is never substituted.
Recursive candidate discovery does not follow symlinks and is bounded by depth 8, 4096 directories, and 64 configs. This is documented as bootstrap behavior, not authoritative family mapping.

reproduction.instructions: Run tests/test_workspace_binding.py and the bounded neutral-CWD enter/start/status/stop run for workspaces A and B.

summary: Explicit workspace resolution is now shared by continuous enter/start/status/stop and works from a neutral CWD for two distinct configured workspaces without cross-attachment. Tests also prove mismatch, ambiguity, and no-config failures are precise and never fall back to CWD. Discovery remains a bounded bootstrap walk (depth 8, 4096 directories, 64 configs); authoritative workspace-to-project mapping is still outstanding.

workaround.description: The mature machine-native workspace identity to authoritative environment/project mapping is still absent; current bounded recursive discovery is the bootstrap resolver.
